name: Low Earth Orbit & SSO
radiationEnvironment: Geomagnetically shielded below Van Allen belts (0.5 - 1.5 krad/year). South Atlantic Anomaly SEU hotspot.
description: Earth orbit between 200 km and 800 km altitude. Sun-synchronous orbits leverage J2 gravitational oblateness to maintain permanent daylight illumination angles across revisits.
scienceGoals: Continental vegetation indices & agricultural drought monitoring
Real-time wildfire propagation tracking and thermal boundary mapping
High-resolution multispectral land surface classification

name: Geostationary Earth Orbit
radiationEnvironment: Outer Van Allen belt electron fringe (5.0 krad/year). Moderate unshielded solar flare exposure.
description: Circular equatorial orbit at 35,786 km altitude with a period matching Earth's sidereal rotation. Spacecraft hovers over a fixed terrestrial longitude with 24/7 continuous line-of-sight.
scienceGoals: Continuous hemispheric weather radar and hurricane storm tracking
High-bandwidth inter-satellite and deep space communications relay
Space weather particle and magnetic field monitoring

name: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1
radiationEnvironment: Unshielded interplanetary solar wind and solar energetic protons (3.0 krad/year). Constant CME exposure.
description: Gravitational equilibrium point 1.5 million kilometers sunward of Earth. Provides an uninterrupted view of the solar disc and samples the solar wind 15-45 minutes before terrestrial arrival.
scienceGoals: Real-time solar coronal mass ejection (CME) early warning alerts
In-situ solar wind speed, plasma density, and interplanetary magnetic field measurement
Full-disc Earth sunlit climate and ozone monitoring

name: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2
radiationEnvironment: Interplanetary galactic cosmic ray background (3.0 krad/year). Zero Earth trapped radiation.
description: Located 1.5 million kilometers anti-sunward behind Earth. Earth and Sun stay aligned behind the spacecraft's sunshield, providing an ultra-stable deep cryogenic dark environment for deep space astronomy.
scienceGoals: Infrared imaging of first-generation cosmic dawn stars and galaxies
Atmospheric transit spectroscopy of temperate habitable-zone exoplanets
Cosmic Microwave Background anisotropic structure mapping

name: Cis-Lunar & Low Lunar Orbit
radiationEnvironment: Solar cosmic rays + lunar surface albedo secondary neutrons (2.0 krad/year). No magnetospheric shield.
description: Low circular polar orbit at 100 km altitude above the Moon. Gravitational mascons cause rapid orbital evolution requiring periodic active orbital maintenance.
scienceGoals: High-precision laser altimetry topographic mapping of polar craters
Epithermal neutron detection of subsurface hydrogen/water-ice deposits
Artemis crewed landing site certification and slope hazard analysis

name: Lunar South Pole Landing
radiationEnvironment: Extreme unshielded solar particle events (SPE) and secondary regolith neutrons. Cryogenic PSR thermal traps (<40K).
description: Powered descent and soft touchdown near the lunar South Pole (Shackleton / Malapert plateau). Extreme low-angle grazing solar illumination with permanent shadows in crater floors.
scienceGoals: Direct drill sampling and isotopic analysis of volatile water ice in PSRs
In-situ regolith seismic activity and thermal conductivity profiling
Autonomous landing obstacle avoidance validation on rough crater rims

name: Mars Transfer & Orbit
radiationEnvironment: Interplanetary galactic cosmic rays during cruise + unshielded Martian solar wind (1.5 - 2.5 krad/year).
description: Heliocentric hyperbolic transfer across 225 million kilometers followed by propulsive capture into Low Mars Orbit. Solar flux is reduced to 43% of Earth levels, demanding enlarged solar arrays.
scienceGoals: Atmospheric loss rates and solar wind stripping dynamics via UV spectroscopy
Sub-meter stereo imaging of paleolakes, deltas, and ancient riverbeds
High-gain telecommunications relay for robotic rovers on the surface

name: Jovian Moon Europa Flyby
radiationEnvironment: Extreme relativistic trapped electrons in Jupiter's magnetosphere (>300 krad/year behind titanium vault).
description: Outer solar system trajectory into the intense radiation belts of Jupiter to perform multi-pass flybys of ice-covered moon Europa. Solar flux drops to 3.7% of Earth, requiring ultra-large arrays or RTGs.
scienceGoals: Ice-penetrating radar sounding of outer brittle ice shell thickness
Surface composition mapping for salts, organics, and active plume cryovolcanism
Induced magnetic field confirmation of a global sub-surface liquid ocean
